elements.title: In 2018:
elements.location: middle of page, full width shaded/framed callout box below the introductory text
elements.content:
In 2018:

• About half of countries (n=92 of 174, 53%) report having national design standards for separating pedestrians and cyclists from motorized traffic (see Fig. 25).

• 76% of countries (n=132 of 174) report having national design standards for the provision of safe crossings for pedestrians and cyclists.

• 64% of countries (n=112 of 174) report having national design standards for the management of speed.

• Less than half of countries (n=70 of 174, 40%) report national design standards that address all three road safety criteria (separating pedestrians and cyclists from motorized traffic; safe crossings for pedestrians and cyclists; and design to manage speed).

• Over three quarters of countries (n=139 of 174, 80%) report having a national strategy for road safety, but of these, only 18% (n=25 of 139) report the strategy to be fully funded; 76% (n=106 of 139) report only partial funding for the strategy (see Fig. 26).
